prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on B043 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The first-round exchange strengthened the scientific case rather than weakening it. The line from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect, through the active peptide, to drugs with independently confirmed cardiovascular and renal benefit is mechanistically stable, mature and not premature. The round-1 files show no scientific dispute on the discovery itself. The dispute is confined to the third name. Holst (human incretin physiology) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology and receptor action) are certain. For the third slot I weigh the question the chair raised, whether the prize rewards a discovery or a drug programme, in favour of the discovery. The identification of the biologically active truncated peptide is the step that made incretin-based therapy conceivable, so I keep Mojsov. The citation says openly that it recognises physiology and the active form, and that the therapies were enabled by those discoveries.
statement.case_against: The weakness is still credit. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form is contested, with Habener and colleagues outside the credited list, and I cannot settle that from the supplied text. I do not treat the unanimity of our round-1 files as evidence that the trio is right, because it shows only that we converged from the same opening ballots. Omitting Knudsen leaves out the person most responsible for liraglutide and semaglutide, and a prize that honours the physiology but not the drug can be called incomplete. Sandberg is also right that GLP-1 may be almost too obvious, and that a single GLP-1 prize uses all three slots and leaves no room for a second discovery. I accept these costs. I do not think they outweigh the strength of the discovery or the clarity of the physiology-centred framing.

responses.point: Svenningsson has moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and asks that the omission of Knudsen be noted openly and not treated as costless.
responses.response: I welcome the move, and I agree the omission is not costless. The chair's question on whether Knudsen should take the third slot if Mojsov's priority is insecure is the right test, and the supplied evidence does not settle it. My answer is that an unresolved priority dispute is a qualification and not a disqualification. The active peptide is part of the discovery chain, whereas analogue design builds on a mechanism others had already established. I would change position only if the primary literature showed that the active form was identified first by someone outside the credited names, in which case the committee should revisit the trio and not simply substitute Knudsen. I also support your wording on the citation: it should state that the physiology and the active form enabled the therapies, so that the omission is deliberate and visible.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps Mojsov over Knudsen unless the priority evidence is stronger than the opening ballots suggest, and says that if Knudsen were included the citation should say plainly that it recognises translation to long-acting agonists.
responses.response: Your condition is fair and I share it. I also accept your correction of the record on my own position: in round 1 I raised Knudsen as a question and I now state plainly that my configuration names Mojsov. Your point that a two-sided tension between concept, engineering and clinical proof recurs in CAR-T is one I accept. It is why I treat B019 as an alternative and not as a co-prize, since Eshhar's early chimeric receptor is outside the credited names. For B043 I would not adopt a translation-framed citation, because that would shift the prize toward one company's compounds and invite the same claim from developers of imatinib or venetoclax. Keeping the citation on physiology and the active form is the more consistent standard.

responses.point: Linnarsson prefers a physiology-centred trio, says Knudsen is the natural third name only if Mojsov's priority cannot be defended, and notes that he relies on recollection of the priority record.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of your conditional position, and with your caution about recollection, which applies equally to me. Where I would add something is on what would change my view. A credible challenge would need primary-literature evidence that the active truncated peptide and its insulinotropic action were established by others before or independently of Mojsov, and that her contribution was confirmatory. Absent that, citing a disputed history is not enough to remove her. I also note your reservation that anti-TNF is widely used but leaves out antibody and cytokine contributors. I accept that, and it is the same attribution risk I would apply to any very mature candidate, including ones not on this shortlist.

responses.point: Sandberg argues that GLP-1 may be almost too obvious, that a single GLP-1 prize leaves no room for the unfolded protein response (B032), and that near-unanimous first places do not settle attribution.
responses.response: I agree that opening support is not merit and that attribution must be argued on its own terms, which is why I have stated the Mojsov and Knudsen costs explicitly. On whether B032 should displace or accompany B043, I keep B043 ahead. The UPR is a conceptually complete pathway with a tidy two-name credit, but Ron, Kaufman and the PERK and ATF6 arms sit partly outside Walter and Mori, and disease-level evidence for modulating it is still early. GLP-1 has demonstrated effects in very large patient populations. A two-part prize would force Mojsov or another GLP-1 name out of a trio that is already contested, and I would not trade a defensible GLP-1 allocation for a split. I would hold B019 and B013 as my next candidates, and I would not object to B032 being held for a later year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide against Habener and colleagues would hold under primary-literature review, which I cannot settle from the supplied text.
Whether the committee prefers a physiology-centred citation or one that names the therapies, which decides the Knudsen question.
If GLP-1 is awarded, whether CAR-T or cGAS-STING is the better candidate to hold for a later year, given Eshhar's omission from B019 and the early therapeutic translation of B013.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. My field is autoimmunity and type I interferon biology, so I have scientific interest in cGAS-STING (B013) and CAR-T (B019), both held only as alternatives, but I have no documented personal or institutional tie to any credited name. Shared Karolinska affiliation with other members is not a recusal issue. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
